senses.definition: (intransitive) To violate rules in order to gain, or attempt to gain, advantage from a situation.
examples: My brother flunked biology because he cheated on his mid-term.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To be unfaithful to one's spouse or partner; to commit adultery, or to engage in sexual or romantic conduct with a person other than one's partner in contravention of the rules of society or agreement in the relationship.
examples: My husband cheated on me with his secretary.
After he found out his wife cheated, he left her.

quotes.text: While the nonavoidant passive-aggressive cheats for the sexual gratification and tries to disguise his or her cheating afterwards, in contrast, the passive-aggressive avoidant cheats less for the sex than to send a message[…]

senses.definition: (transitive) To avoid a seemingly inevitable thing.
examples: He cheated death when his car collided with a moving train.
I feel as if I've cheated fate.

senses.definition: (transitive) To deceive; to fool; to trick.
examples: My ex-wife cheated me out of $40,000.
He cheated his way into office.

quotes.text: I am subject to a tyrant, a sorcerer, that by his cunning hath cheated me of this island.

senses.definition: (informal, intransitive) To disregard self-imposed restrictions or commitments in favour of resting or indulging oneself.
(countable) An act of deception or fraud; that which is the means of fraud or deception.
